newsitem.title: USA: STOCK PRICES SOAR ON POSITIVE ECONOMIC DATA.
newsitem.headline: STOCK PRICES SOAR ON POSITIVE ECONOMIC DATA.

text.p: The stock market soared in early trading on Wednesday as Wall Street welcomed a set of better-than-expected reports on the economy, including the seventh straight monthly drop in producer prices.

Shortly after 10:00 a.m. EDT(/1400 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average, which had been under the gun for the last few sessions in anticipation of bad economic news, was up 54.35 points at 8,015.19 after jumping nearly 80 points initially.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 17.22 points at 1,593.46.
The rally followed a government report that the Producer Price index -- one of the key gauges of inflation -- dropped unexpectedly for a record seventh month in a row in July
The PPI was off 0.1 percent, following an identical drop in June. Without the volatile food and energy components, wholesale prices also fell by 0.1 percent.
Wall Street analysts surveyed by Reuters had expected prices to rise by 0.1 percent last month.
In a separate report, the Commerce Department said July retail sales were up a moderate 0.6 percent last month, reflecting a broadbased improvement in all businesses except furniture.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.7 percent rise in overall retail sales.

The reports will be among the data considered by Federal Reserve policy-makers next week when they decide whether economic growth is strong enough to require a rise in interest rates in a pre-emptive move against inflation.
The inflation-sensitive bond market also reacted strongly, with the benchmark 30-year bond up a full point, sending its yield down 6.59 percent from 6.67 at Tuesday's close.
"These numbers (both retail sales and the PPI) should be looked at very positively by markets," said Sam Stovall, an analyst at S&P Industry Reports.

"If they came in as expected, there would have been no surprise," he said. "But since they came in lower than expected, we should have a very nice day in the market today. Both indicators show inflation is not a concern."

The stock market had staggered lower over the last few sessions, with the Dow driven down 101 points on Tuesday and below the 8,000-point level for the first time in three weeks on concern that the economic reports would point to accelerating growth.
On Thursday, the government will also report on inflation at the consumer level for July, but few analysts expect any bad surprises after Wednesday's upbeat producer price data.
